---
title: "The rendering pipeline"
---

Rendering is where `post.qmd` stops being text and becomes the **block list**
everything else keys off: its heading, its paragraph, and its code cell, each a
separate block with its own identity. The entry point is
`render_document_with_includes(src, base_dir)` in `render/mod.rs`; it runs a fixed
sequence of stages, each a small, testable function.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
  src[".qmd source"] --> inc["includes::resolve<br/>{{< include >}} + source map"]
  inc --> sc["expand_shortcodes<br/>extension {{< name >}} templates"]
  sc --> spans["scan_div_spans<br/>record ::: fenced divs"]
  spans --> pre["preprocess<br/>blank ::: markers (line-preserving)"]
  pre --> ast["comrak parse_document<br/>(+ sourcepos)"]
  ast --> walk["walk top-level nodes<br/>→ FlatBlock (emit HTML, hash id)"]
  walk --> group["group_divs<br/>rewrap into callouts/columns"]
  group --> cite["table captions + cite::process<br/>citations, @refs"]
  cite --> blocks["RenderedDoc { blocks, title, … }"]
```

## Stage by stage

1. **Include resolution** (`includes.rs`). `{{< include path >}}` shortcodes are
   expanded inline, and a `Vec<LineOrigin>` source map records, for every line of
   the expanded text, which file + line it came from. Cycles are detected and left
   in place. This is what makes click-to-source work *across files*.
2. **Shortcode expansion** (`render/extension/`). `{{< name args >}}` tags
   declared by the active format extension expand to their HTML templates. It is
   **line-preserving** (each tag opens and closes on one line, the template's
   newlines collapsed) so the source map from stage 1 stays valid.
3. **Fenced-div scan + preprocess** (`render/divs.rs`). Quarto's `:::` divs aren't
   CommonMark, so their spans are recorded first, then the marker lines are blanked
   *without changing the line count* (again preserving sourcepos). The inner
   content then parses as ordinary blocks.
4. **Parse** (`comrak`, with `sourcepos` on). One AST for the whole document, with
   every node carrying its `startLine:col-endLine:col`.
5. **Walk → FlatBlock** (`render/mod.rs` + `render/emit.rs`). Each *top-level* node
   becomes one block: the emitter renders it to HTML (code highlighted by
   `highlight.rs`, math by `math.rs`), and the block gets a **content-hash id**
   (`b-<hex>`, with a positional tiebreak for duplicates) and a `data-sourcepos`
   mapped back through the source map. A `` ```{lang} `` fence is recognised as an
   executable **cell** and recorded for the server to run later. The front-matter
   node is where metadata, the theme, and a format extension's includes are
   resolved.
6. **Regroup divs** (`render/divs.rs`). The flat blocks are wrapped back into
   callout / layout-grid / generic container blocks using the spans from stage 3.
   Inner blocks keep their own ids and sourcepos, so click-to-source works inside a
   callout.
7. **Captions + citations** (`cite.rs`). Table captions are numbered, then
   `[@key]` citations and `@fig-`/`@sec-`/… cross-references are resolved against
   the bibliography and the cross-reference registry.

The result is a `RenderedDoc`: an ordered `Vec<Block>` plus the title, theme, TOC
flag, includes, and any non-fatal `warnings`.

## The block contract

Every emitted block carries three data attributes, and **the whole system depends
on them** (`crates/core/tests/corpus.rs` enforces it):

- `data-block-id` — a content hash. Because it's content-derived, an unchanged
  block keeps its id across edits and is never touched by the diff.
- `data-sourcepos` — the original source range (drives click-to-source).
- `data-source-file` — present only on blocks pulled in from an include.

## Citations & cross-references

Citations and cross-references (`cite.rs`) are the last pipeline stage, and they
run as a **post-process over the already-rendered block HTML**: they transform only
plain-text runs, never the inside of a tag, code, or math span, so block sourcepos
is left untouched. `[@key]` citations become numbered links to a References block
appended to the document (the one structural change), formatted from the parsed
BibTeX. `@fig-` / `@sec-` / `@tbl-` / `@eq-` references become links to their anchor,
carrying the resolved number when it is known. It is deliberately **pragmatic, not
a full CSL engine**. Cross-*page* references (a `@fig-` that lives in another
chapter) are resolved a layer up, in the site subsystem (see [The multi-page
subsystem](sites.qmd)).

## Incremental updates

On a save the server re-runs the pipeline and calls `diff_blocks(old, new)`
(`diff.rs`): an LCS over the block-id sequences finds the stable anchors, and the
gaps between them become `Update` / `Insert` / `Remove` ops. Only those ops cross
the websocket, so the browser swaps a handful of elements while everything
else — including live canvases — stays put. (Code-cell *outputs* are blocks too,
keyed to the cell id, so re-running a cell updates only its output block.) Our
`tau` edit is the smallest case of all: only the cell's code changed, so the cell
re-runs and its output block re-renders, while the heading and the paragraph keep
their ids and are never touched.

## Output assembly

A `RenderedDoc` becomes a full page through one assembler, `render/page.rs`
(`assemble_html_page`): it wraps the block HTML in the document shell, the `<head>`
theme script, the bundled offline assets, and, for an OJS page, the Observable
runtime. A deck routes through `render/reveal.rs` instead, and a site/book page adds
chrome from `site/`, but the **same assembler builds the page shell for the static
`build` and for both live-preview servers** (preview just injects the websocket
client into that shell), so they can't drift apart. The same block list backs all
three outputs (see [Architecture](architecture.qmd)).

## Interactive cells (OJS)

Observable (`ojs`) cells are client-side reactive, not kernel-executed, so they sit
outside the [execution](execution.qmd) path. Two decisions keep them cheap and
robust. The page assembler ships the Observable runtime **only when a page actually
contains live cells** (`page.rs`'s `has_ojs`), so a page without them carries no
runtime weight. And because every OJS cell is a block with a content-hash id, an
unedited cell is **never touched by the diff**, so a reactive graph keeps its
runtime state across a save, the same live-state guarantee a Three.js canvas gets.
